Class EditDialog

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.dialog.EditDialog
public final class EditDialog extends Object
Builds a modal dialog that edits a copy of something and writes it back only on Save (7.3.0): a title, your controls, Cancel and Save. The same shell as ConfirmDialog (an ordinary Panel, the modal flags set, centered, as wide and as tall as its content) with your controls where the confirm's body is.

The copy is yours, the draft. Your controls are lenses onto it, so nothing the player does in the dialog touches the real thing. Open the dialog by filling the draft from the item and setting the state its visibility reads; Save runs onSave, which writes the draft to the item and closes it; Cancel and Escape run onCancel, which closes it, and the draft is dropped (the next open fills it again). As with ConfirmDialog, the dialog keeps no state of its own and does not close itself. 

private @Nullable String editing;              // the item the dialog edits, null while closed
private final Draft draft = new Draft();       // the copy it edits

Panel editDialog = EditDialog.builder()
    .title(() -> Component.literal("Edit " + items.get(editing).name()))
    .content(Flow.builder().vertical().gap(4)
            .add(TextField.builder().size(160, 20).state(() -> draft.name, v -> draft.name = v).build())
            .build())
    .onSave(() -> { items.get(editing).setName(draft.name); editing = null; })
    .onCancel(() -> editing = null)
    .build()
    .visibleWhen(() -> editing != null);

// Open it from your own button, on a row, say:
Button.builder().label(Component.literal("Edit"))
    .onClick(() -> { draft.name = item.name(); editing = item.id(); })
    .build();
Add the Panel where a ConfirmDialog goes: to an MKScreen's panels, or to another screen through ScreenPanelAdapter.
